stories.title: We are a spoiled fanbase and it shows
stories.summary:
The number of people complaining about Allen’s play is disturbing. You're spoiled.



	 



	The Bills offense put up 406 yards today and scored 26 points. It would have been 29 if Bass didn't shank a kick.



	 



	Allen threw for 304 yards on 60% passing, and his receivers didn't help him. In the first half, Allen hit Shakir right in the stomach on a ball that would have given us 1st and goal at the 5. Dropped. Coleman dropped another one that would have been first down. It was a tougher catch, but still catchable. In the second half, another ball went right through Moore's hands around the 5.



	 



	Some say Allen struggled from the beginning: I disagree. If Shakir catches just his ball (give Coleman a pass since his was a tough one), Allen would have had 106 yards in the first quarter alone. That's a 424-yard pace for the game. 



	 



	His one truly head-scratcher of a throw, the INT across the middle, came right after he took a forearm shiver to the head. It should have been a penalty.



	 



	For context, the Bengals, with the best WR room in the league and the hot-shot offense, put up 307 yards against this same Dolphins defense. We had over 400. Burrow threw for 190. Allen threw for 304. Burrow had 5.9 yards per attempt against this Dolphins D. Allen had 7.3 …



	 



	Allen is a QB who rides the highs more than most. If the offense gets into a rhythm, he's going to go off in historic fashion. But if the offense struggles around him, he can slump too. It's those failures around him that really derail him.



	 



	That's why I've rallied for years to get him more receiving help. Adding Moore was not enough. 



	 



	Relax. Allen is fine. But I maintain that he still needs better weapons.

Game #24 Preview & Open Thread: Buffalo Sabres at Tampa Bay Lightning
stories.summary:
Thunderbolts and Lightning, Very Very Frightning



Buffalo Sabres (9-10-4) at Tampa Bay Lightning (15-5-2)



Puck Drop: 5 p.m. ET | Benchmark International Arena, Tampa, Florida



TV: MSG-B, DAZN, NHL Network, NHL Center Ice



Radio: WGR 550, Sirius XM (app)



Know Your Opponent



Tampa Bay Lightning



Record: 15-5-2 | 32 Pts



Last Game: 3-1 victory over the Oilers



Division Ranking: 2nd 



PP: 19th, 21.1% (Sabres: 30th, 16.0%)



PK: 23rd, 73.7% (Sabres: 26th, 72.2%)



Season Series: The Sabres are 0-1-0 vs Tampa this season.



*Please note the early 5pm ET start of the game*



1. Avoid Another Tampa Bay Beatdown



It was just eleven days ago when the Lightning hammered the Sabres in their own building by an 8-3 score. Both Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen and Colten Ellis were lit up, and the team took an embarrassing beating on the scoreboard. The emotional toll was just as damaging, leaving Buffalo with plenty to think about after such a humbling performance.



Since then, Tampa Bay is firing on all cylinders, currently sitting in second place in the Atlantic Division. Ottawa moved a point ahead of the Bolts last night, but has also played two more games. Head coach Jon Cooper’s team continues to play great hockey, as usual. The Lightning have also enjoyed two days off since putting the brakes on Connor McDavid and the Oilers with a convincing 3-1 victory.



Meanwhile, Buffalo enters this matchup on the second night of a back-to-back, while Tampa Bay is well-rested. No favors from the NHL here. The Sabres played a solid two periods on the road last night before unraveling against the Panthers. They’ll need a much better 60-minute effort if they hope to keep pace with this Lightning team.



The interesting thing is that the Sabres actually had Tampa Bay’s number last year. Buffalo finished the 2025-26 regular-season series with a 3-0-1 record against the Lightning, winning three of the four meetings. (while inching out the division title) That makes this season’s opening 8-3 drubbing at the hands of the Bolts all the more frustrating. What happened to the team that seemed to have Tampa figured out just a year ago?









2. Lightning Strike Early and Often



Tampa is averaging nearly four goals per game, a clear indication of just how dangerous this offensive group remains. Through their first 20 games, the Lightning had scored 54 five-on-five goals, third-most in the NHL. They were also 11th in the league in fewest five-on-five goals allowed. Their established stars continue to lead the offensive charge, with Nikita Kucherov (31 points), Jake Guentzel (27 points) and Brandon Hagel (24 points) setting the pace.



Tampa Bay is already playing like a legitimate contender. Jon Cooper has an experienced, balanced group that knows what it takes to win. The Lightning have done a good job limiting dangerous scoring opportunities around their own net, although their overall defensive numbers still leave some room for improvement. Andrei Vasilevskiy remains a stalwart between the pipes, posting a 2.59 GAA through 17 games.







Photo Credit: Sabres.com



3. Injury Status



The Lightning are a little banged up, with two quality players currently on IR. Brandon Hagel missed Tampa Bay’s previous game and is expected to sit out today’s contest as he continues to recover from a lower-body injury. His absence will be significant, as Hagel has already contributed 13 goals this season.



Conor Geekie is also sidelined after being placed on IR with an undisclosed injury and is expected to miss at least a week.



Old friend Zemgus Girgensons is listed as day-to-day with an upper-body injury, making his availability for today’s game uncertain.



Aside from the longer-term injuries to Justin Danforth and Matt Grzelcyk, Buffalo is relatively healthy right now. Konsta Helenius remains week-to-week, but he has recently resumed skating, which is an encouraging sign.



Ryan McLeod and Louis Crevier were healthy scratches on Saturday. We could see one or both return to the lineup today if head coach Lindy Ruff wants to get some fresh legs on the ice against Tampa Bay. No lineup changes have been announced as of this writing, and the final decisions won’t be officially confirmed until pregame warmups.

stories.title: Sloppy third period costs Sabres in 4-3 loss to Panthers
stories.summary:
Sam Bennett’s hat trick leads Florida to big divisional win



Box Score



Score: Florida Panthers 4, Buffalo Sabres 3Shots: FLA 30-19 BUF



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Jiri Kulich 3 (Benson, Thompson), Jack Quinn 12 (Zellweger, Metsa), Tage Thompson 15 (Samuelsson)Florida Panthers Goals: Sam Bennett 8 (Vilmanis, Gudas), Sam Bennett 9 (Luostarinen), Sam Bennett 10 SH (Jones, Reinhart), Sandis Vilmanis 4 (Bennett, Jones)



Quick Thoughts



First Period – Cool from Kulich



The Sabres found themselves down just three minutes into the game, as a sloppy line change let Sam Bennett enter the zone, dance around Rasmus Dahlin and beat Alex Lyon to give Florida a 1-0 lead.



After giving up the early goal, Buffalo had the better of the chances for the rest of the period.



First, Noah Ostlund sent in Jack Quinn on a breakaway, who went five-hole on Panthers goalie Jacob Markstrom, but the puck went out the other side and into the corner. A few minutes later, a strong forecheck by Tage Thompson set up Jiri Kulich point blank, but Markstrom made a great save.



That wasn’t the last chance Kulich would have, though. Just about halfway through the period, Thompson hit Zach Benson with a cross-ice feed, who then sent in Kulich one-on-one with Markstrom. The Czech went backhand, forehand and managed to force the puck underneath Markstrom’s pad to tie the game, 1-1. 




Beauty of a play all around. Kulich, 1-1 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlaPanthers pic.twitter.com/7b5a1N2UT1— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) November 21, 2026




Tyson Kozak took a high-sticking penalty 23 seconds after the goal, but Buffalo managed to keep a hot Panthers power play at bay.



Kulich finished the first period with four shots on goal in what felt like his most active 20 minutes of the season, but the Sabres and Panthers remained tied 1-1 after the first.



Second Period – Back-and-forth



Kulich had his legs going again early in the second, as a stretch pass sent him in on a breakaway, but this time Markstrom got the better of the 22-year-old.



A fantastic shift from the Kulich line pinned the Panthers in deep, and eventually led to Quinn picking up the puck. Quinn danced around the blue and let loose a shot from the high slot that went off the post and in, giving Buffalo a 2-1 lead just over five minutes into the second.




Jack Quinn nasty wristshot, 2-1 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlaPanthers pic.twitter.com/VsgNBceq1B— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) November 22, 2026




As has been a common occurrence this season, though, the Sabres’ lead did not last long. Just 18 seconds later, Bennett rounded the net, shrugged off Noah Ostlund and beat Lyon from the slot to tie the game again. Lindy Ruff made a questionable challenge for goaltender interference, as a Panthers skater was battling with Olen Zellweger at the side of the net, but it was unsuccessful.



Buffalo’s penalty kill did a good job ensuring the penalty for the failed challenge didn’t snowball into another Florida goal.



The Sabres came inches away from retaking the lead, as Owen Power threw a puck toward the net that deflected off Benson’s torso, off the crossbar and out the other side — all the while Markstrom knew nothing about it.



Mattias Samuelsson took a questionable holding penalty with under two minutes left in the period, but a Florida penalty 30 seconds into the kill evened things up at 4-on-4. During that spell, Gustav Forsling and Carter Verhaeghe both had great opportunities, but Lyon stood tall to keep the score 2-2 heading to the third.



Third Period – Outworked



Bennett completed his hat trick less a minute into the third period, which ended up being a shorthanded goal as it came seconds after the 4-on-4 concluded. Sam Reinhart found a trailing Bennett in the high slot, and his shot caught a piece of Lyon’s glove, but had enough to find the back of the net, making it 3-2 Panthers. The puck may have been deflected by Power on its way through, but it’s one Lyon should have had.



A failed clearing attempt led to Florida getting pinned in their own end again, but Dahlin’s one-time effort from the point was saved by Markstrom who pushed across.



After a sluggish start to the period, the Sabres’ top goalscorer came through again to flip the script. Thompson picked up a pass at center ice and sped down the near wing before ripping a 90 mph wrist shot that beat Markstrom at the near post, tying the game 3-3 with just over 11 minutes left in the period.



The Panthers had been the better team throughout the third, and got rewarded for it with three minutes to play. Buffalo’s fourth line got caught out on a long shift, and were forced to ice the puck twice. Off the second faceoff, Bennett ripped a shot from the high slot that hit a body in front, and fell perfectly to Sandis Vilmanis, who tucked it in the open net and gave Florida the lead for good.




Sam Bennett's shot gets blocked and goes right to Vilmanis for him to slam it in, 4-3 #LetsGoBuffalo #FlaPanthers pic.twitter.com/U9EDoBsS2m— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) November 22, 2026




It’s fair to question why the fourth line, along with Zach Metsa and Olen Zellweger, were even on the ice in that late game situation. In the end, it cost the Sabres an important, early season divisional game, as Buffalo mustered no quality chances with the net empty.



At The Horn



This game was marred by turnovers and poor clearances by both teams, and it felt like two points were there for the taking for whoever wanted it. 



Well, judging by that third period, the Panthers wanted it much more.



The Sabres were outshot 11-3 in the final period and looked lifeless on offense. They now trail Florida by seven points in the wild card race, and should be incredibly disappointed with that effort as a follow-up to Thursday’s win in Washington. If there’s any positive to take, the Benson-Thompson-Kulich line was fantastic and should get some more looks. On the other hand, Buffalo’s bottom six was invisible once again, and the fourth line wound up costing them late. 



With such a short turnaround against a Lightning team that comes in on two days rest tomorrow, it felt like the Sabres needed a win in Sunrise tonight.



So much for that.




NHL Game Score Impact Card for Buffalo Sabres on 2026-11-21: pic.twitter.com/NAOEIEXtYF— HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) November 22, 2026




Next Up



The Sabres return to action in less than 24 hours, as they make the short trek to Tampa Bay for another divisional game against the Lightning. Puck drop is set for 5 p.m.

Buffalo looks to gain ground in the Atlantic Division



Buffalo Sabres (9-9-4) at Florida Panthers (12-8-3)



Puck Drop: 6 p.m. ET | Amerant Bank Arena, Sunrise, FL



TV: MSG-B, WSFL-TV 39Radio: WGR 550, Sirius XM (app)



Know Your Opponent

Division Ranking: 5th



PP: 11th, 24.2% [Sabres: 30th, 16.4%]



PK: 6th, 84.3% [Sabres: 26th, 71.1%]



Season Series: Sabres 1-0-0 vs. Panthers



What to Watch



1. Can Dahlin stay hot?



It’s been a quiet start to the season for Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin, which has been one of many contributing factors to the team’s slow start. However, the 26-year-old had his best game in weeks during Thursday’s win against the Capitals.



Dahlin tallied a goal, an end-to-end beauty finished on a wrap around, and an assist to help Buffalo end its 5-game losing streak. Heading into a tough, divisional back-to-back in Florida, the Sabres could use more of that out of their captain.



Fortunately, Dahlin has played well against the Panthers of late. He has seven points in his last six games against Florida, including a goal the last time these two teams met, a 5-3 Sabres win in October.



2. Benson’s remarkable start



It’s not farfetched to say that the Sabres’ best line this season has been, simply, whatever one has Zach Benson on it.



The 21-year-old forward has continued his trajectory as one of Buffalo’s most important players following his electrifying postseason play last season. He leads Sabres skaters with an xGF% of 56%, and is tied for first on the team with 14 assists.



While the goals haven’t quite been there yet, it’s not for a lack of chances. His 5.6 goals below expected is tops on the Sabres by a significant margin. While he does practically everything else, the one aspect of Benson’s game that has long been below average is his shooting.



After scoring his third goal of the season Thursday against Washington, we’ll soon see if Buffalo’s chaos agent can go on a bit of a scoring run.



*Stats via HockeyStats.com



3. One Tkachuk, two Tkachuk



With the Panthers down two big pieces in Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, it’s been the Tkachuk brothers leading the way for Florida.



In particular, it’s been Matthew doing most of the damage recently. The eldest brother is riding a 9-game point streak, and has 12 total in that span. Meanwhile, Brady has nine points in his last nine games.



If Buffalo can keep the brothers quiet, it would go a long way toward securing an important two points.



Injury Notes



While Marchand and Barkov are both very close to returning for the Panthers, according to head coach Paul Maurice, neither will play against the Sabres on Saturday. Both have been out since early October with knee injuries.



Sabres coach Lindy Ruff mentioned during Saturday morning’s media availability that “a couple” players were banged up following Thursday’s game against Washington, but did not specify who or their status for Saturday’s matchup. Something to keep an eye on as warmups near.

stories.title: State of the NFL game
stories.summary:
Even with the Bills playing a lot of prime time games, I still enjoy getting NFL Sunday Ticket because I like watching other games.  This season, somewhat because of injuries to star players (Hurts, Maye, Puka, etc.) and unexpected poor play by some teams (Chargers, Houston) I’m finding there are a lot of unattractive games.



	 



	Looking at this week’s games, I know it’s affected by 6 byes including 4 teams with winning records, you had Thursday’s game of Indy at Houston.  Yuck, I didn’t watch a second of it.  Other matchups: Tennessee/Dallas, New Orleans/Chicago, Arizona/KC, Jets/Chargers.  They don’t interest me at all and I play a lot of fantasy football.



	 



	Fortunately, Sunday night has the best matchup of the week with Minnesota and the Niners.



	 



	Again, I know the byes affect this a lot, and they’re stretched out over 9 weeks, but I’m starting to see a dilution of good NFL games from my perspective.



	 



	I’ve seen a few of you say that other than Bills games, you prefer watching college football.  Normally during the college football season, I watch UB games and, living in Northern California, I watch Stanford, Cal and San Jose St, all of which are mediocre this season.   I’ve noticed that there are a lot of matchups each week between Top 25 teams.  I guess I may be missing out on watching better football.



	 



	One issue I do have with college sports was brought on by NIL money and the transfer portal.  The players are changing teams too much.  Gone  is the interest in watching teams being built and grow together as a team.  The result is you’re just watching the game for the entertainment, which is fine.



	 



	 I’m curious if anyone else is finding NFL Football losing its appeal.   It doesn’t help that generally the first couple weeks have some poor quality football because teams don’t play starters in the preseason.

stories.summary:
Boxscore



Score: Buffalo Sabres 6–3 Washington CapitalsShots: BUF 18–36 WSH



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Quinn (Östlund, Dahlin); Dahlin PPG (unassisted); Malenstyn (Carrick, Kozak); Benson (Krebs, Power); Thompson PPG (Quinn, Doan); Quinn ENG (Power).



Washington Capitals Goals: Tuch (unassisted); Leonard PPG (Tuch, I. Protas); Jenner (Ovechkin, A. Protas).



Quick Thoughts



Finally, Some Breathing Room



This recap was a lot more fun to write than the last few, for sure. The Sabres needed a win, and for once they gave themselves enough offense early to withstand a rough stretch late. Sam Carrick and Tom Wilson dropped the gloves one second into the game. Buffalo followed with four first-period goals, starting with Jack Quinn at 5:25. Rasmus Dahlin doubled the lead, and Beck Malenstyn scored just 25 seconds later to make it 3–0. Washington pulled Logan Thompson after he allowed three goals on five shots. That was the kind of start Buffalo had been missing during its five-game slide. Creating chances only helps if somebody finishes them. Thursday, the Sabres made their early opportunities count.



An Answer for Tuch



Of course Alex Tuch scored against his former team. His unassisted goal brought Washington within two just 43 seconds after Malenstyn’s tally. The chemistry between Tuch and Thompson is still there, with basically passing it right to Tuch for the giveaway before Tuch sniped it. But Zach Benson answered at 15:55, finishing at the doorstep to restore Buffalo’s three-goal cushion before the intermission. Benson’s goal mattered beyond making it 4–1. Buffalo had already watched promising leads disappear during this stretch. Answering Washington before the break kept the Capitals from carrying a little more hope into the second.



Nine Seconds Made a Difference



Tage Thompson scored on the power play with nine seconds remaining in the second period, sending Buffalo into the third ahead 5–1. Quinn and Josh Doan collected the assists. It was Buffalo’s second power-play goal of the night, with the unit finishing 2-for-3. That fifth goal ended up being valuable insurance. A four-goal lead should be comfortable with 20 minutes left. For these Sabres, there was still some work to do.



Still Had to Make It Interesting



Ryan Leonard scored on the power play at 8:52 of the third. Boone Jenner followed 52 seconds later, and suddenly Washington was within two with more than half the period remaining. Buffalo eventually settled the result when Quinn hit the empty net with 43 seconds left. The finish offered a reminder that Buffalo’s problems haven’t disappeared. Washington doubled the Sabres in shots, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen had to stop 33 of 36 to protect the win. Six goals look great on the scoreboard, but Buffalo still asked plenty of its goalie.



At The Horn



Quinn finished with two goals and an assist, Dahlin contributed a goal and an assist, and Owen Power added two helpers. Buffalo got scoring from five different players and finally ended its five-game losing streak. There is plenty to clean up, especially when protecting a lead. But the Sabres needed two points, and they earned them without having to recover from another early deficit or take their chances in overtime. UPL was good enough and made some big saves, even though he would probably want those three goals back. This resembled last year’s team, and now they need to build a streak as they head to Florida for Saturday’s game against the Panthers. One win gets the road trip moving. Building on it would make this feel like the start of something.

Sabres desperate to stem bleeding against old friend

Money for Nothing



Last season for the Buffalo Sabres saw Dire Straits carry a completely different connotation from this season. Last season, it signified a rallying cry. This year, it is what they find themselves in. 



Losers of five consecutive games, a span in which they have only picked up one point in the standings, the Buffalo Sabres are reeling. They are not shooting the puck, not finishing when they do, and not generating enough offense. Their goaltending is also not bailing them out, and beyond that, are collectively still largely proving inconsistent at best and ineffective at worst. 



Even a lengthy road trip, the savior of last year’s team, has had this squad only dig themselves deeper. And as they approach the end of the trip before returning home for two games, they will square off yet again with a familiar face, in Alex Tuch. While there seems to be some dispute about just how things went down between Tuch and the Sabres before he was traded to his new home, the fact of the matter is that he is gone and on paper, they could certainly use his contributions for this season. 



Tuch is gunning for Jacob Misiorowski’s crown this season, tallying 12 goals through 19 games on the season, which would put him second on the Sabres, but only has two assists, though distribution was never his hallmark. On a contribution basis, the 2026/27 Sabres could use this goal scoring. They have several natural distributors that could be setting up Tuch at a similar clip, and while Tuch has a track record of being a bit of an inconsistent finisher, the lack of being able to find nylon is discussed at length. The team almost certainly misses his locker room leadership as well.



But for all of that said, the discussion that has broadly happened around Tuch is moot. Whether you believe the team did not make a competitive offer or that Tuch wanted to leave regardless of the offer, the fact is that he’s a Washington Capital. Constant discourse about whether or not they should have tried harder to get him to stay, which evokes a similar feeling to say, a goalie in New Jersey or a different one in Edmonton, he’s not on the roster and dwelling on that fact doesn’t do anyone any good. It’s an easy, low-hanging talking point, but an exhausting and fruitless one. 



Whether or not the team misses his contributions and leadership is moot, and while it is pretty undeniable that they do, we should be able to look forward. Hopefully after the Sabres and Capitals meet tonight, the Tuch discourse can be put to bed for a bit, at least until he has his homecoming in March. 



Diamonds in the rough



It is pretty well established that Sabres GM Jarmo Kekalainen is big game hunting. He’s been trying to do it since he took over the role of Sabres’ General Manager, being in on Colton Parayko, Robert Thomas, Connor Hellebuyck, and most recently Dylan Larkin. And while the splashy acquisition could certainly inject some life into the team, the cautionary tale of the big move could be on the opposing bench tonight for the Sabres.



The Washington Capitals had the darling off-season, acquiring Tuch, Jordan Kyrou, and Boone Jenner to bolster the forward unit, along with Vincent Desharnais to shore up the blue line. Despite all these acquisitions, the Capitals find themselves in just about the same spot in the standings as the Sabres, albeit with two less games played with two extra wins. 



Thus far, it has not been the torrid start the Capitals and their fans may have expected given those acquisitions, and while it can take a team with multiple big additions some time to gel, a lot of their flaws are flaws that the Sabres share. They are in the bottom third of the league in penalty kill and in just about the same territory on the power play. They do finish at a better clip than the Sabres do, and while goalie Logan Thompson is struggling a bit to start the year, you’d be hard pressed to find a Sabres fan who wouldn’t happily trade goalie situations with the Capitals. 



The Capitals, along with some other teams, can serve as a bit of a cautionary tale that the big fish isn’t always the right one. Where he could look for an example instead is with last year’s Pittsburgh Penguins. Struggling for a spark, they acquired a disgruntled Columbus Blue Jackets winger in Egor Chinakhov, who was stifled on playing time and saw him absolutely catch fire, putting up 36 points in 43 games, helping to spark a run that saw the Penguins finish second in the Metro division. 



While there is an allusion to be drawn here to another Columbus winger stifled on playing time in Dmitri Voronkov, it’s more to serve as a broader point that the right move doesn’t have to be the big one. The Sabres are gasping for air when it comes to contributions from all of their wingers not named Jack Quinn or Zach Benson, and whether it’s Voronkov or someone else in a similar vein, any acquisition could help spark a turn around. Kekalainen doesn’t even need to look outside the organization for examples of this, he could instead look inward at his own acquisition of Olen Zellweger, who has been a reliable piece of the Sabres blue line. That is similar to the presence they need to see added to the forward group. 



But whether it’s Voronkov, Rickard Rakell, Ivan Miroshnichenko, or someone bigger, the Sabres very clearly need help and the longer Kekalainen sits on his hands and watches, the more he will be compared to his predecessor. The fairness of that comparison is irrelevant, the inaction is what matters.

stories.summary:
Lack of Leadership Continues to Plague the Sabres



The Buffalo Sabres are a young team, chock-full of talent. They have seemingly been that way for some time now, as a new batch of prospects emerges every few years. A few stick with the team and find varying degrees of success, while others move on and seem to improve their odds of succeeding elsewhere.



For this article, though, I’m going to focus on the here and now: the current 2026-27 Buffalo Sabres.



There is no denying the talent assembled on this roster, but the results on the ice are often downright underwelming. This team struggles to function as a cohesive unit and frequently looks rudderless in the vast ocean of the NHL. I’ve come to believe that a significant part of the problem is a lack of leadership.



It often comes up among Sabres fans and DBTB readers that this team lacks the veteran presence and physicality needed to compete night in and night out. While I certainly agree there is validity to that argument, leadership comes in all shapes and sizes. And in my opinion, the Sabres’ youth doesn’t have leadership qualities in their character. They are looking for a leader and it is not among them. It is also lacking among the veterans on the team.



When you look at the greatest leaders in NHL history, many of them were also the driving forces behind some of the league’s most successful teams. They had a way of elevating everyone around them, bringing out the best in their teammates and demanding accountability. Mark Messier, Ray Bourque, Bobby Clarke, Jonathan Toews and Gordie Howe come to mind. These were elite players who led by example and set the standard for everyone else.



And you didn’t necessarily have to be a big-time scorer to be an effective leader, either. Bob Gainey, Patrice Bergeron and Scott Stevens were legendary leaders in their own right. They demonstrated that hard work, commitment, sacrifice and accountability can be every bit as important as putting points on the scoreboard.



There is no single statistical requirement or formal performance threshold for NHL leadership. It’s generally determined by a combination of character, accountability, communication, work ethic, experience, and the ability to influence teammates. When you examine Buffalo’s current roster, very few players come close to meeting this criteria.







Here is a breakdown of what to look for in a team leader:



1. Accountability




Takes responsibility for mistakes rather than blaming teammates, coaches, or circumstances.



Admits when he hasn’t played well.



Holds himself to the same standards he expects from everyone else.



Leads by example when things aren’t going well.




2. Work ethic and commitment




Consistently gives maximum effort, regardless of the score.



Plays hard in practice, not just on game night.



Demonstrates discipline and preparation.



Doesn’t take nights off or disappear when the team faces adversity.




3. Leads by example




Plays the right way, even when it’s uncomfortable.



Competes defensively as well as offensively.



Is willing to block shots, win battles, backcheck, and do the dirty work.



Sets a standard that younger players can follow.




4. Communication and influence




Communicates effectively with teammates.



Isn’t afraid to speak up when something needs to be said.



Can motivate teammates without embarrassing or belittling them.



Earns the respect of the locker room, rather than demanding it.




5. Mental toughness and composure




Remains composed when the team is struggling.



Doesn’t allow frustration to affect his game or attitude.



Responds positively to adversity.



Helps teammates maintain confidence during losing streaks and difficult stretches.




6. Team-first mentality




Puts team success ahead of personal statistics and recognition.



Celebrates teammates’ accomplishments.



Makes sacrifices for the betterment of the team.



Doesn’t put himself above the organization or the team’s objectives.




NOTE: This six point leadership criteria list was taken off Google. This was the inspiration for the article.



The Sabres continue to have more passengers than drivers on this team. Buffalo’s current crop of “leaders” generally pales in comparison to those on most other teams around the league.



Captain Rasmus Dahlin is probably held in the highest regard within the organization and among his teammates, but his standing isn’t quite as lofty around the NHL. Rasmus has his share of warts that hold him back from being considered an elite leader. Undisciplined penalties, inconsistency, and questionable defensive play are just a few examples. Not to mention all the losing that has gone on during his watch.







With that in mind, here is my personal tier list, ranking the impact each player has as a leader on this Buffalo roster. Your rankings may vary, and that’s perfectly fine. However, I think most fans would agree that this team is lacking when it comes to leadership, particularly when compared to the rest of the league.



Tier 1 – Elite Leaders: Players who lead by example, command respect, hold teammates accountable, and elevate everyone around them. 



Nobody.



Tier 2 – Strong Leaders: Dependable veterans who demonstrate leadership qualities but may not have the complete package. 



Dahlin



Tier 3 – Developing Leaders: Players who show leadership potential but haven’t fully established themselves as influential voices. Or players who are who they are at this point.



Krebs, Benson, Samuelsson, Power, Doan, Thompson, Zucker, Lyon, Malenstyn, Norris, Quinn, Kozak, Carrick, Zellwegger, Ellis. Metza, Timmins



Tier 4 – Followers: Players who contribute to the team but don’t demonstrate meaningful leadership qualities.



McLeod, UPL, Ostlund, Kulich, Helenius, Crevier



Tier 5 – Leadership Void: Players who actively fall short of leadership expectations or negatively influence the team’s culture.



Thankfully none.



As you can see, most of the team falls somewhere in the middle tiers. Nothing particularly special and certainly nothing to write home about. I placed Krebs at the top of Tier 3 because he is a vocal presence in the locker room and on the bench, and a great teammate. His consistency on the ice isn’t always there, however, and he rarely makes a significant impact on the scoresheet. Still, his effort is unquestionable, as is his fighting spirit. He’s a bit of a mixed bag, but that makes him the second-best leader on this team in my opinion. And that’s a problem when your second-best leader is only good enough for Tier 3.



I have UPL ranked lower because of his inconsistency this season and his tendency to let things snowball when things aren’t going his way. The young trio of Noah Ostlund, Jiri Kulich and Konsta Helenius have the potential to develop into team leaders. However, they are still finding their footing in the NHL and have plenty of growing to do before they can assume those responsibilities.



We all know Buffalo lost Alex Tuch in the offseason. Despite his own inconsistencies, I would have placed him in Tier 2, just below Dahlin. Bo Byram and Jordan Greenway would have ranked higher in Tier 3 as well. That’s a fair amount of leadership, experience, and veteran presence that has now moved elsewhere. The Sabres weren’t exactly overflowing with leadership to begin with, and losing those players only makes the situation worse.



There is no quick fix here, but Buffalo needs to make a concerted effort to start identifying and acquiring players with a higher caliber of leadership. I know Mark Messier and Patrice Bergeron don’t grow on trees, but those are extreme examples. Start drafting the kid who possesses the intangibles you want in a player, not simply the one who skates a little faster and puts up 80 points instead of “only” 65.



Look for players with a relentless spirit and a willingness to battle for their teammates when making trades or signing free agents. A leader doesn’t just want to win, he shows others how to do it. A leader doesn’t win with talent alone, he does it with his integrity and character too.



A true NHL leader sets the standard, holds himself accountable, demands the best from his teammates, and demonstrates through his actions what it means to be a professional. More of that is desperately needed in the Blue and Gold if this team hopes to achieve any measure of sustained success.

stories.summary:
Buffalo blows two leads as November woes continue



Box score



Score: Philadelphia Flyers 4, Buffalo Sabres 3 Shots: Philadelphia 33, Buffalo 19



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Mattias Samuelsson 3 (Dahlin, Doan), Tage Thompson 13 (Benson, Kozak), Jiri Kulich 2 (Thompson)Philadelphia Flyers Goals: Jamie Drysdale 2 (Michkov, Cates), Owen Tippett (Drysdale, Knuble), Travis Sanheim 4 (Dvorak, Barkey), Christian Dvorak 4 (Seeler, Michkov)



Quick Thoughts



First Period – Foot on the gas



The Sabres got off to about as fast of a start as you could want, as Mattias Samuelsson roofed a puck from a tough angle past Flyers goalie Joseph Woll to put Buffalo up 1-0 just 47 seconds into the game. The goal happened thanks to a great battle and keep in from Peyton Krebs.




Mattias Samuelsson asks "You like that?" to someone after scoring a goal with a nice shot, 1-0  #LetsGoBuffalo #LetsGoFlyers pic.twitter.com/V1qRtloYe8— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) November 18, 2026




Tage Thompson had two great looks on the ensuing shift, forcing a save from Woll on a 2-on-1, and shortly after backhanded the puck just wide with a gaping net.



A few minutes later, Jack Quinn used great speed to fly past Oliver Bonk and get in clean on Woll, but couldn’t quite lift the puck over the netminder’s outstretched pad.



Josh Doan took a high-sticking penalty with 11 minutes remaining in the period, but Buffalo successfully killed it off without allowing any dangerous chances.



Sabres goalie Alex Lyon made his best save of the period to deny Sean Couturier, who had a point blank look in the low slot but only found the glove of Lyon with just over five minutes remaining. 



Woll made a great save to keep the Flyers deficit at 1-0, denying Quinn’s backhand effort from the slot with a blocker save. Off the rebound, with Woll sprawled in the crease, Rasmus Dahlin ripped a shot from the point that rung off the crossbar.



Buffalo went to the power play for the final 53 seconds of the period, but probably would have been better off without it, as the Sabres failed to get any consistent zone time. With a second remaining, Noah Cates had a great shorthanded look from the slot after receiving a pass from the corner, but Quinn’s back check broke up the chance.



Despite the poor end to the first, Buffalo played a strong period overall, out-chancing the Flyers 8-3.



Second Period – Hit the brakes



Buffalo’s power play that continued into the second period ended without mustering a shot on goal, and was a sign of things to come.



Shortly after the Flyers’ penalty expired, they began controlling play. Owen Power had a great block to deny a scoring opportunity, and Lyon followed that up with a strong save to deny Travis Konecny.



The Flyers eventually tied the game with 13:21 remaining in the period, as Jamie Drysdale powered a one-timer from the near face-off circle past Lyon.



The Sabres’ first shot on goal of the second came on a Dahlin shot from the point, just under nine minutes into the period.



From seemingly nothing, Buffalo managed to retake the lead. Zach Benson did a great job stealing a puck below the goal line, and he rounded the net to find an open Thompson, who beat Woll with a one-time blast for his team-leading 13th goal of the season, giving the Sabres a 2-1 lead.




Benson –> Thompson, 2-1 #LetsGoBuffalo #LetsGoFlyers pic.twitter.com/RA4qIn2vRV— Buffalo Hockey Moments (@SabresPlays) November 18, 2026




Three and a half minutes later, Philadelphia’s pressure culminated in the tying goal, as Drysdale backhanded a puck toward the net from the point that somehow avoided the sticks of three Sabres, and found Owen Tippett alone on the doorstep for a redirect past Lyon to make it 2-2.



With just about two minutes remaining, Buffalo finally got its cycle going in the offensive zone for its best shift of the period. It culminated in a Noah Ostlund slapshot from the point, which deflected to Conor Timmins, who probably would’ve scored if he wasn’t hooked by Tyson Foerster. 



The Sabres’ power play was short-lived, as Thompson took a high-sticking penalty with 32 seconds remaining in the period to negate the man-advantage.



After coming out of the gates strong, the Sabres looked much like they have throughout their four-game losing streak in the second period.



Third Period – Wheels fall off



In the blink of an eye, the Sabres were trailing for the first time in the game.



While play was still at 4-on-4, Travis Sanheim snuck down from the point, received a cross-ice pass and ripped a shot cross body on Lyon to make it 3-2 Flyers, just 29 seconds into the period.



Lyon kept Buffalo in the game with a big save a couple minutes later, pushing across to deny Tippett on a 2-on-1, and that stop proved big. A minute later, Thompson picked up a loose puck in the high slot and used some silky handles to maneuver around two Flyers, before setting up Kulich for a one-time blast that beat Woll on the glove side, making it 3-3.



The tie was short-lived, however, as Christian Dvorak streaked down the near wing and let loose a shot that found the far corner, giving Philadelphia the lead back, 4-3, less than a minute after Kulich’s tally. It appeared Lyon’s positioning was a bit too low toward the goal line when squaring up to Dvorak, but it was still a pinpoint shot from the veteran forward.




Philadelphia goal!Scored by Christian Dvorak with 14:37 left in the 3rd. Assisted by Nick Seeler and Matvei Michkov.PHI: 4 | BUF: 3#BUFvsPHI #LetsGoFlyers #LetsGoBuffalo pic.twitter.com/4VTwhn1Kyj— NHL Goals (@nhl_goal_bot) November 18, 2026




Just like against Dallas, Buffalo took a killer of a late penalty, as Krebs went to the box for a hook with eight mintues remaining. The Sabres did manage to kill the penalty and keep themselves in the game, despite a couple quality chances for Philadelphia.



With about five minutes to play, Ostlund made a great play at the blue line to gain a partial breakaway, but instead of shooting, opted for a drop pass to Zach Metsa, whose shooting lane was taken away and then couldn’t find a pass to the back post. It was a questionable decision, and wound up being Buffalo’s best look at the goal the rest of the game, as their 6-on-5 mustered nothing and gave Philadelphia a 4-3 win.



Quick Thoughts



We’re now a quarter of the way through the season, and the Sabres are quickly slipping back to mediocrity.



They have now lost five consecutive games, have been outshot all three games of this road trip, and sit seven points out of a playoff spot. A number of players who were counted on to be contributors this season have been pedestrian at best throughout the skid, and frankly, the whole campaign. 



It was yet another negative goals saved above expected performance for a Buffalo goaltender, the Sabres offense mustered just 2.24 expected goals on the night, according to HockeyStats.com, and were outshot 27-11 over the final two periods after a strong first frame. Buffalo is now 0-2-0 against the lowly Flyers this season.



I do have good news or bad news, depending on how optimistic or pessimistic you are: there’s still three quarters of the season left.




NHL Game Score Impact Card for Buffalo Sabres on 2026-11-17: pic.twitter.com/XzWvqCjYr6— HockeyStatCards (@hockeystatcards) November 18, 2026




Next up



The Sabres continue their road trip in Washington, where they’ll face the Capitals at 7 p.m. Thursday.

Kulich has now been promoted to centering the top line with Krebs and Tage separated. Maybe McLeod can benefit from Östlund and Quinn’s presence on the third line and if dropping to the fourth line won’t fire up Zucker, what will?



2. Do Something Darcy Jarmo



We are at the quarter mark of the season and the Sabres’ funk is real. Their point-per-game pace will not make the playoffs, especially with the Atlantic once again looking super competitive. The playoff ship has not sailed, but Buffalo cannot afford to fall further adrift. 



To that end, Jarmo Kekäläinen came to Buffalo with a reputation for being a gunslinger when making trades. However, so far he’s been a lot more patient and low-key, which then makes us wonder, is that because he’s being cautious at the beginning of his term, or has he been told to keep his powder dry by the powers that be above him?



3. Philly-Nilly Defense



The Flyers vs Sabres encounters tend to be explosive goalfests, with Buffalo going 6-4-0 in the last ten games they have played. The four goals scored in Philly’s 3-1 win earlier this season was the fewest in the last 12 games they have played going back to March ’23. stories.title: Stars Align in Dallas as Sabres are Shutout Again, 2-0
stories.summary:
Buffalo Has No Goals, No Mojo, No Identity and No Chance



Score: Buffalo Sabres 0-2 Dallas StarsShots: BUF 22-30 DAL



Buffalo Sabres Goals: You had a better chance of spotting Bigfoot tonight.Dallas Stars Goals: Benn 4th (Hryckowian, Lundkvist) Johnston 4th PPG (Rantanen, Hintz)



Plus 1: Keeping it Even on the Road



Alex Lyon made his second consecutive start since returning from injury. He was tested early as Dallas came out applying the pressure. Buffalo was a little sloppy moving the puck out of its own zone, and the Stars took advantage of the turnovers, outshooting the Sabres 4-0 before Tage Thompson finally registered Buffalo’s first shot on goal.



Dallas took the game’s first penalty though, but (hold onto your hats) the Sabres couldn’t do a thing with the man advantage. They failed to register a single shot and never really managed to get anything set up. Another wasted power-play opportunity.



Buffalo started to get their legs moving a little more, generating a few chances before Jiri Kulich’s slashing penalty put a halt to the momentum. Wyatt Johnston of Dallas was called for hooking shortly afterward, sending the teams into a 4-on-4 situation for nearly a minute and a half. The Sabres’ abbreviated power play managed to generate a shot on goal, but nothing more.



Lyon then came up with a huge stop on Jason Robertson, who had gotten behind the Buffalo defense for a dangerous chance in tight. However, Zach Benson was called for slashing on the play, giving Dallas its second power-play opportunity of the night. The Sabres responded with a defensive clinic, actually looking like a competent penalty kill for a change. Buffalo successfully killed it off and immediately went to work with a power play of its own. That went about as well as you would as expected.



No score after one period of play, with the Stars holding the territorial advantage. Shots on goal favored Dallas 10-6. Kudos to Jiri Kulich for delivering the defensive play of the period. His backcheck on an odd-man rush by Dallas prevented a quality scoring chance. It’s nice to see the young player stepping up and taking more responsibility in his own end.







Minus 1: How Come We Never Score?



Buffalo came out strong to start the second period, generating some good sustained pressure with an aggressive forecheck. However, Jiri Kulich took his second penalty of the game, this time for holding in the offensive zone, giving Dallas its third power-play opportunity. The Sabres were once again up to the challenge, keeping the Stars off the scoreboard.



The Stars began to reestablish their territorial advantage, but Alex Lyon remained solid between the pipes. A glove save from the slot and a dangerous bank shot from behind the net by Jamie Benn were the highlights. Lyon hugged the post and squeezed his pads together to keep the puck out.



Halfway through the game, Lyon and his counterpart, Jake Oettinger, both had goose eggs on the scoreboard. Oettinger had the easier time of it, however, with Lyon facing 17 shots compared to just nine for the Dallas netminder.



Lyon was tested again with just under four minutes remaining in the period, standing his ground and using excellent positioning to thwart a great Dallas scoring opportunity. But as fate would have it, Jamie Benn, who was closing in on his 1,000th NHL point, would find the back of the net on a rebound after a tipped shot to put Dallas up 1-0. Lyon had no chance after making a terrific initial save. Isn’t that just the way of things? It seems like half the milestones in NHL history are achieved against Buffalo.



After two periods, the Sabres were being outshot 20-11 and had been held scoreless for four straight periods, dating back to the first period in Chicago. Even worse, Jake Oettinger had now kept Buffalo off the scoreboard for five consecutive periods. He was also in net for the Stars’ 4-0 victory in Buffalo earlier this season.



Nearly half of Buffalo’s forwards hadn’t even registered a shot attempt at this point in the game. Outside of a few brief flashes, the Sabres had been mostly stagnant and listless, struggling to generate any offense against Dallas’ tight defensive coverage. It was becoming increasingly difficult to see where a goal was going to come from.



Minus 2: Impotent Offense



Buffalo came out with a much better start to the third period, seemingly showing some motivation for the first time in a while. Rasmus Dahlin had a golden opportunity to unleash a shot from about 20 feet out, but held onto the puck too long, allowing a sliding Dallas defender to get in his way. Dahlin tried to shake wide but couldn’t find a teammate with a pass.



Josh Doan then had a great opportunity in the slot after a puck steal, only to have Jason Robertson slash his stick in half, drawing a penalty. The much-maligned Buffalo power play had yet another chance to make something happen and came damn close when Noah Östlund got a great opportunity in tight. But, as has been usual, Jake Oettinger was there to shut the door.



The penalty box parade continued, as Rasmus Dahlin and Thomas Harley were each sent off for slashing before Dallas was called for tripping Jack Quinn. Buffalo had plenty of open ice with a 4-on-3 advantage for over a minute. The Sabres moved the puck around beautifully but couldn’t find the perfect shooting lane they were looking for. Tage Thompson unleashed one of his patented shots from the faceoff dot, but Jake Oettinger was all over it.



The Sabres then shifted into overdrive, throwing everything they had at the Dallas net. Zach Benson had the best opportunity, sending a shot/pass into the crease, but Oettinger was able to tip it away. Buffalo was finally generating some serious pressure, but the Dallas netminder continued to stand in the way.



Buffalo pulled Lyon late in a desperate attempt to tie things up, and the Sabres applied some strong offensive pressure. But Zach Benson then made a costly, thoughtless play, bowling over Jake Oettinger from behind as the Dallas goaltender played the puck. The result was a late power play for the Stars.



The Sabres’ penalty kill, which had been perfect and arguably one of the team’s strongest aspects all evening, finally cracked. Wyatt Johnston scored his fourth of the season to put the game away for Dallas. 









The Sabres fall 2-0 to the Stars, and Buffalo finishes the season series SCORELESS in two games as Dallas completes the sweep. Six periods without a goal against the Stars and five consecutive scoreless periods overall. The forwards obviously need to start finishing their chances, as half the team seems snakebit right now. But the defensemen deserve their share of the criticism, too. Buffalo has invested heavily in its offensive blue line, particularly in highly paid Rasmus Dahlin and Owen Power. Those contracts come with expectations, and the production needs to justify the investment. Not much from Mattias Samuelsson or Olen Zellweeger lately either.



Photo Credit: Sabres.com



Final Thoughts:



Another wasted effort for Buffalo’s netminder as the Sabres simply can’t find a timely goal. Alex Lyon was outstanding for most of the night, but his teammates had absolutely no answers offensively. Lyon gave Buffalo every opportunity to win this game, stopping 28 of 30 shots in another strong performance, but the Sabres continue to come up empty when it matters most.



It’s been an alarming lack of finish lately, and the frustration is mounting. A disappointing night all around for the organization and its fans. The Sabres have now dropped four straight and five of their last six games.



If you can stomach it, the road trip continues as Buffalo heads to Philadelphia for its next game on Tuesday night, November 17th, against the Flyers. Game time is 7:00 PM.

stories.title: Next three games quite possibly the key to our entire postseason dreams.
stories.summary:
To me the most absurd and sad stat of the Josh Allen era Bills teams is them being the only team out of four teams to win a playoff game in six consecutive seasons and not win a Super Bowl. Of course, the stat is even worse than that though as we all know. Those other three teams didn't just win a Super Bowl but they were dynasties that won 3 super bowls. And the Bills haven't just not won a Super Bowl, they haven't even been to a Super Bowl.



	 



	The next failure would be the Bills inability to secure the 1 seed. They have had the talent to do so for six straight seasons now dating back to 2020. And this isn't just a "Chiefs problem" as during that six-year span, the Chiefs have only secured the 1 seed in three of those seasons. Titans, Ravens and Broncos were the other three teams to come away with the one seed in the years the Chiefs floundered. 



	 



	A win Monday against the Vikings would put the Bills in a spot they have never been in the Josh Allen era. A 7-1 conference leading record after 8 games played. To my knowledge the Josh Allen led Bills have never a) had sole possession of 1st place in the conference at that point or later in the season and b) have also never tallied 7 wins in their first 8 games played. I feel like over the last seven seasons the Bills have been 6-2 too many times to count. In fact, they were even 6-2 in 2019 before Josh Allen broke out. But they have never achieved that 7-1 record.



	 



	Win on Monday night and then beat the Jets and Dolphins to get to 9-1. No excuses. Just execute and do it. The current era Bills so far have never been able to hold such a record or complete such a task. They've always found a way to stumble. Specifically, the McDermott led Bills seemed to always find a way to lose two consecutive games in either October or November. Well, October has come and gone and by the skin of his teeth, Brady was able to avoid losing two consecutive in the month of October. 



	 



	If the Bills can enter the Thanksgiving game against the Chiefs at 9-1, they will have on paper 5 tough games left. If they can go 3-2 in those games, I think they almost assuredly lock up the 1 seed. Only going 2-3 opens things up as both Cincy and Jacksonville have pretty easy schedules the rest of the way. Jacksonville in particular would have to drop a game or two they "should win on paper". 



	 



	One thing seems for certain though, if the Bills don't take care of business in these next three games, I and really none of us should take them seriously for the 1 seed. I don't know if it's simply bad luck or misfortune as the Bills have certainly had multiple 3 loss seasons now and failed to obtain the one seed, but bottom line is sometimes you simply have to have a ridiculous 1 or 2 loss season to get the one seed. And if that is the case they certainly can't afford to drop either of the next three games with the upcoming slate of games that starts on Thanksgiving.
